items.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500 slip after CPI data raises Fed rate-hike bets
items.take: October CPI came in hot: +0.4% on the month with core +0.3%, both above forecasts, and there is still no official year-over-year number because of the shutdown. Stocks opened lower with the Nasdaq down most, and traders now overwhelmingly price a December hike, with a growing cohort calling for a 50-basis-point jumbo.

items.title: Stock Market Today (Nov. 10, 2026): Nasdaq falls after key inflation report
items.take: The hot print sets the stage for another hike in December after Monday's relief rally. Fed Governor Waller, speaking in London before the report, said even a cool October would not have changed his vote for a quarter-point hike, and that a 50-basis-point move should be considered if core ran 0.3% or more. It ran exactly 0.3%.

items.title: CPI Live Updates: Inflation Persists in U.S. Economy
items.take: The Fed's favorite gauge, supercore services, rose 0.4% in October, running near 5.5% annualized over the past three months. The Times' own back-of-envelope math puts year-over-year inflation around 4%, though it cautions that figure is partly a shutdown artifact.

items.title: Hotter-than-expected October CPI weighs on U.S. stocks
items.take: Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1% and S&P futures 0.4% ahead of the open, with Dow futures flat. Off the macro wire: Microsoft is lobbying the administration to scrap a planned ban on Chinese AI data-center parts.

items.title: CPI Report Shows Core Prices Up 0.3% Again, Hitting Waller's Line for Weighing a Half Point Hike
items.take: Core prices matched Waller's stated threshold for considering a half-point December move, but strategists like Principal's Seema Shah pushed back: an outsized hike needs evidence inflation is accelerating decisively, and 'we are not there yet.' Falling gasoline prices gave consumers the one bright spot.

items.title: Investors Weigh Fallout from Nvidia Spy Scandal
items.take: Today's rotation pick, fresh this morning: WSJ's What's News digests the CPI print alongside the Nvidia spy-scandal fallout that knocked the chipmaker out of Monday's rally.
